$comment: PRICE BOOK — edit this file to publish prices on the website.
WHY THIS MATTERS: Google shows price-rich snippets for shopping queries, and Ugandan
customers search 'iPhone price in Uganda', 'how much is an iPhone 13 in UGX' and similar.
A product with no price here publishes NO price and NO Offer structured data, which makes
it ineligible for product rich results and merchant listings.
HOW TO ADD A PRICE:
Add an entry under 'products' keyed by the product id (the /products/<id>/ slug).
"iphone-17-pro-max": { "price": 6200000, "condition": "new", "availability": "InStock" }
FIELDS:
price        - number, in the currency below. Whole units (no separators). REQUIRED.
priceHigh    - optional number. Set it when the model spans a range across storage tiers;
'price' is then treated as the lowest configuration price.
condition    - 'new' | 'refurbished' | 'used'. Default 'new'.
availability - 'InStock' | 'OutOfStock' | 'PreOrder' | 'LimitedAvailability'. Default 'InStock'.
note         - optional short string shown next to the price (e.g. '256GB, sealed').
RULES:
- Only publish prices the shop will actually honour. A wrong price is worse than none:
Google penalises mismatched prices and customers lose trust.
- Update 'updated' whenever you change prices.
- Leave a product out entirely if its price is not settled. The page still builds and
still says 'ask for today's price' — it simply gets no Offer markup.
- Run 'npm run build' after editing. The build prints how many products have prices.
